text.p: The main stories in the Austrian press this Thursday are:
- Styrian People's Party official Gerhard Hirschmann laid out his proposals to replace Austrian provincial parliaments with three new regions of east, west and south.
- Bonn says Austria can join NATO any time it wants as it is a special case.
- The European Union Commission has now formally launched proceedings against Austria over the toll on the Brenner Alpine route.
- Industry. More flexible work times should check associated wage costs. Industrial Union chief Peter Mitterbauer says there will be no rise in real wages.
- Bank Austria has sold off its 12 percent stake in cement maker Perlmooser to French firm Lafarge.
- The trial of Andreas Goldberger for alleged cocaine abuse has been postponed until Autumn from August as originally planned.
- Grocers will try to win back customers from supermarkets by expanding their services to sell lottery tickets, provide photocopying facilities and postal services.
- The postal savings bank does not want to give up its lucrative share in the lottery.
- Lenzing sees a rosier year ahead in 1998 and expects to come back into profit figures.
- Food chain Julius Meinl is cutting 500 jobs as part of a restructuring and cost saving plan to try to improve profits.
- The social ministry wants to update the employment law to create more jobs for the disabled. The government must be a role model in this field.
- Cheap shopping is on the rise. Discount shops are luring more customers across Europe.

- The consortium around EVN, Verbund and Wienstrom have serious competition in the race to buy a 25 percent stake in energy plant OKA. The Styrian energy firm is allowed to join forces with a foreign firm.
- Creditanstalt securities experts give the stock markets further upside potential, particularly the European bourses, including Vienna.
